description: We are a team from Cairo University, Faculty of Engineering, who are passionate about making a real impact.
summary: School-age children often hear about ongoing space missions, but what about the missions that have long been abandoned? Our project aims to address this lack of awareness among school-aged children. We have created a website that teaches students about the Opportunity rover, which once roamed the Martian surface. Our website uses 3D models to give users a unique visual experience and includes interactive elements to make learning more engaging. Our project can also be expanded to include other abandoned equipment through the 'Coming Soon' section on the website, which currently includes the Spirit rover.
details:
Problem Definition:
The problem revolves around the lack of the spark of imagination and storytelling needed to capture a younger or more casual audience's attention when it comes to how information on past missions and achievements is presented. This matters because these probes, rovers, and spaceships have contributed so much to human knowledge over the years, and their legacy must be honored.

Our Solution:
We built a website that tells the story of the Opportunity rover (or Oppy) in an engaging and simplified manner suitable for school-aged space enthusiasts. Our goal was to create an emotional, authentic experience that follows Oppy throughout its mission on Mars, showcasing both the achievements and the hardships the rover faced. What makes our website unique is the use of 3D models, which provide an interesting look, and the interactive story elements, which make the experience more interesting and engaging, making the user more involved in the storytelling experience. The website uses HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, along with the Three.js library for integrating the 3D models into the website.

The 3D Models

Some of the 3D models were sourced through the NASA 3D resources, while the rest were made from scratch by our 3D artist, like the rocket and capsule. Only one of the models, Mars with water, was sourced from a free-to-use 3D model, which our 3D artist later modified to fit the aesthetic of the project.

The Interactivity

The interactive elements involve building the capsule in which the rover is placed, launching the rocket, and moving the rover using arrows in various contexts. The interactive elements are easy to grasp, and the instructions are worded in a clear manner.

The Voiceover

Every main story scene is voiced over to improve accessibility. Hearing the story read aloud makes the experience more immersive and helps those with disabilities like dyslexia consume the content on the website more easily.

The Story

The project presents the story in a simplified and engaging way. The story begins by stating the mission for the twin rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, and follows the Opportunity rover from launch aboard the Delta II rocket until its arrival on Mars. It then talks about Opportunity's discoveries and the difficulties it faced along the way. It highlights how the discoveries made by the rover helped scientists answer the mystery of ancient water on Mars.

Options for Further Development

While our project currently focuses on Opportunity, we've included a 'Coming Soon' section featuring its twin, the Spirit rover, which explored the opposite side of Mars. Because the site is built to easily expand with more inspiring stories of Martian exploration, this flexibility sets us up for continuous growth and future updates. Other options for updates might include the Ingenuity helicopter, the Sojourner rover, which was the first wheeled vehicle to operate on Mars, or even derelict Martian orbiters. There is also an option to expand beyond Martian missions by adding a section for derelict equipment currently residing on the Moon.
